title: Prime Minister heads to COP31 to press for climate finance
excerpt: Tarique Rahman is in Antalya from 10 to 12 November and will meet the UNDP Administrator and several leaders. His plenary speech is on the last day.
content:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman leaves for Antalya, Turkiye, on Tuesday, 10 November, for the high-level segment of the UN climate summit COP31, bdnews24.com reported. He will stay until 12 November and address the plenary on his last day.

Who he will meet

  • Confirmed: the Prime Minister of Australia, the President of Uzbekistan and the Vice President of China.
  • Scheduled: the UK Foreign Secretary and the UNDP Administrator.
  • Possible: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

State Ministers for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir and Shama Obaed Islam are travelling with him.

The message

Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury told reporters on 9 November that compensation for climate impacts remains an open issue. Developed countries committed under the Paris Agreement to support countries like Bangladesh with finance and technology, he said, but that support is not always delivered, so Bangladesh is pushing for it collectively with other vulnerable countries.

He described the trip as a courtesy visit rather than a bilateral one, and said substantive decisions were unlikely there.

Bangladesh’s negotiators are asking for a threefold increase in adaptation finance and for adaptation and loss and damage money to come as grants, not loans. Read our COP31 explainer.

Why it matters

The meeting with the UNDP Administrator matters most for the development sector. UNDP is one of the main channels for climate adaptation money in Bangladesh, and its funding has been squeezed by donor cuts. Any announcement on climate funds or partnerships could shape programmes run with NGOs in coastal and flood-prone districts.

What to watch

The prime minister’s plenary speech on 12 November, any outcome from the UNDP meeting, and whether Bangladesh joins new funding announcements during the leaders’ segment.
